about: The words of the Backtest Blocks strategy language. Functions, series, calendar and position values go in conditions; settings are "key: value" lines; words are the rest of the rule language. A parameter or definition name is letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore, and is not one of "reserved".

functions.name: sma
functions.summary: simple average of the last n closes
functions.text: Simple average of the last n closes. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in sma(volume, 20).

functions.name: ema
functions.summary: exponential average
functions.text: Exponential average that starts from the simple average of the first n values. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in ema(volume, 20).

functions.name: rsi
functions.summary: relative strength index, 0 to 100
functions.text: Relative strength index, 0 to 100, from Wilder averages of the up and down changes. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in rsi(volume, 14).

functions.name: roc
functions.summary: change in n bars, as a fraction
functions.text: Change in n bars, as a fraction: compare it with a percentage, as in roc(20) > 5%. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in roc(volume, 20).

functions.name: stdev
functions.summary: standard deviation of the last n closes
functions.text: Standard deviation of the last n closes, with division by n. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in stdev(volume, 20).

functions.name: highest
functions.summary: highest high of the last n bars (add [1] to remove this bar)
functions.text: Highest high of the last n bars, this bar included (add [1] to remove this bar). It reads high, or the series you write first, as in highest(volume, 20).

functions.name: lowest
functions.summary: lowest low of the last n bars
functions.text: Lowest low of the last n bars, this bar included. It reads low, or the series you write first, as in lowest(volume, 20).

functions.name: atr
functions.summary: average true range
functions.text: Average true range, as a Wilder average. It has no series argument.

functions.name: macd
functions.summary: fast average minus slow average
functions.text: The fast exponential average minus the slow one. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in macd(volume, 12, 26).

functions.name: macd_signal
functions.summary: average of the macd line
functions.text: Exponential average of the macd line, with a period of signal bars. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in macd_signal(volume, 12, 26, 9).
functions.example: buy when macd() crosses above macd_signal()

functions.name: bb_upper
functions.summary: upper Bollinger band
functions.text: Upper Bollinger band: the average plus width standard deviations. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in bb_upper(volume, 20, 2).

functions.name: bb_lower
functions.summary: lower Bollinger band
functions.text: Lower Bollinger band: the average minus width standard deviations. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in bb_lower(volume, 20, 2).

functions.name: stoch_k
functions.summary: stochastic %K, 0 to 100
functions.text: Stochastic %K, 0 to 100: where the close is in the high-low range of the last n bars, averaged across smooth bars (1 for none). It has no series argument.

functions.name: stoch_d
functions.summary: stochastic %D: the d-bar average of stoch_k
functions.text: Stochastic %D: the d-bar average of stoch_k, with the same n and smooth. It has no series argument.
functions.example: buy when stoch_k() crosses above stoch_d()

functions.name: adx
functions.summary: average directional index, 0 to 100
functions.text: Average directional index, 0 to 100: the strength of the trend, up or down, as the n-bar Wilder average of 100 * |plus_di - minus_di| / (plus_di + minus_di). It has no series argument.
functions.example: buy when adx(14) > 25 and plus_di(14) > minus_di(14)

functions.name: plus_di
functions.summary: plus directional indicator, 0 to 100
functions.text: Plus directional indicator, 0 to 100: 100 times the n-bar Wilder average of the up movement, divided by that of the true range. It has no series argument.

functions.name: minus_di
functions.summary: minus directional indicator, 0 to 100
functions.text: Minus directional indicator, 0 to 100: 100 times the n-bar Wilder average of the down movement, divided by that of the true range. It has no series argument.

functions.name: cci
functions.summary: commodity channel index of the typical price
functions.text: Commodity channel index: the typical price (high + low + close) / 3 minus its n-bar average, divided by 0.015 times its mean absolute deviation from that average. It has no series argument.

functions.name: williams_r
functions.summary: Williams %R, -100 to 0
functions.text: Williams %R, from -100 to 0: -100 * (highest high - close) / (highest high - lowest low) of the last n bars. It has no series argument.

functions.name: mfi
functions.summary: money flow index, 0 to 100
functions.text: Money flow index, 0 to 100: 100 - 100 / (1 + up flow / down flow) of the last n bars, with flow = typical price * volume. It has no series argument, the ticker must have volume, and the flow of a bar is up when its typical price increased.

functions.name: obv
functions.summary: on-balance volume, a total of volume
functions.text: On-balance volume: a total, 0 on the first bar, that adds the bar volume when the close increases and subtracts it when the close decreases. It has no series argument, and the ticker must have volume.

functions.name: vwap
functions.summary: volume-weighted average price of the last n bars
functions.text: Volume-weighted average of the typical price (high + low + close) / 3 of the last n bars. It has no series argument, and the ticker must have volume.

functions.name: keltner_upper
functions.summary: upper Keltner channel
functions.text: Upper Keltner channel: the n-bar exponential average plus width times the average true range of the last atr bars of the ticker. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in keltner_upper(volume, 20, 2, 10).

functions.name: keltner_lower
functions.summary: lower Keltner channel
functions.text: Lower Keltner channel: the n-bar exponential average minus width times the average true range of the last atr bars of the ticker. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in keltner_lower(volume, 20, 2, 10).

functions.name: supertrend
functions.summary: supertrend line, below the price in an uptrend
functions.text: Supertrend line: the lower band in an uptrend, the upper in a downtrend, at (high + low) / 2 minus or plus mult n-bar average true ranges. It has no series argument, and a band only moves nearer to the price until the close crosses it.

functions.name: supertrend_up
functions.summary: condition: the supertrend is in an uptrend
functions.text: A condition: true when the supertrend is in an uptrend (its line is below the price), and false in a downtrend. It has no series argument.

functions.name: wma
functions.summary: weighted average of the last n values
functions.text: Linear weighted average of the last n values: the newest value has the weight n, and each bar before it has 1 less. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in wma(volume, 20).

functions.name: hma
functions.summary: Hull moving average
functions.text: Hull moving average: the sqrt(n)-bar weighted average of twice the (n / 2)-bar weighted average minus the n-bar one, with n / 2 and sqrt(n) rounded down. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in hma(volume, 20).

functions.name: median
functions.summary: median of the last n values
functions.text: Median of the last n values: for an even n, the average of the two middle values. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in median(volume, 20).

functions.name: zscore
functions.summary: standard deviations from the n-bar average
functions.text: How many standard deviations the value is from the average of the last n values, with stdev (division by n), unknown when all are equal. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in zscore(volume, 20).

functions.name: percent_rank
functions.summary: percentage of the previous n values less than this one
functions.text: The percentage of the previous n values that are less than this value, from 0 to 100. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in percent_rank(volume, 20).

functions.name: slope
functions.summary: least-squares slope of n bars, per bar
functions.text: Slope of the least-squares line through the last n values, in the units of the series per bar. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in slope(volume, 20).

functions.name: correl
functions.summary: correlation with a different ticker, -1 to 1
functions.text: Correlation (-1 to 1) of the last n one-bar changes of the first series and this ticker’s close, unknown if one is constant. It reads close for this ticker, and the series you write first as of reads it, aligned with the bars of this ticker.

functions.name: count
functions.summary: how many of the last n bars a condition held
functions.text: How many of the last n bars the condition held on, this bar included, unknown while one of them is unknown. It has no series argument, only a condition.

functions.name: bars_since
functions.summary: bars since a condition was last true
functions.text: Bars since the condition was last true: 0 on a bar where it is true, and unknown until it is true for the first time. It has no series argument, only a condition.
functions.example: buy when bars_since(close crosses above sma(50)) < 10

functions.name: sum
functions.summary: sum of the last n values
functions.text: Sum of the last n values. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in sum(volume, 20).

functions.name: dema
functions.summary: double exponential average, less lag than ema
functions.text: Double exponential average, 2 * e1 - e2, with e1 = ema(n) and e2 the n-bar ema of e1: it has less lag than ema. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in dema(volume, 20).

functions.name: tema
functions.summary: triple exponential average, less lag than ema
functions.text: Triple exponential average, 3 * e1 - 3 * e2 + e3, with e1 = ema(n), e2 = ema of e1 and e3 = ema of e2 (n bars each): less lag than dema. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in tema(volume, 20).

functions.name: kama
functions.summary: Kaufman adaptive average: fast in a trend, slow in a range
functions.text: Kaufman adaptive average: on each bar it moves sc = (ER * (2 / (fast + 1) - 2 / (slow + 1)) + 2 / (slow + 1)) squared of the distance to the price, with ER the n-bar efficiency ratio. It reads close, or the series you write first, and starts from the value of the bar before the first known ER.

functions.name: aroon_up
functions.summary: aroon up, 0 to 100: 100 on the bar of the high
functions.text: Aroon up, 0 to 100: 100 * (n - bars since the highest high of the last n + 1 bars) / n, with the newest of equal highs. It has no series argument and reads the highs of the ticker.

functions.name: aroon_down
functions.summary: aroon down, 0 to 100: 100 on the bar of the low
functions.text: Aroon down, 0 to 100: 100 * (n - bars since the lowest low of the last n + 1 bars) / n, with the newest of equal lows. It has no series argument and reads the lows of the ticker.

functions.name: psar
functions.summary: parabolic SAR, a stop below the price in an uptrend
functions.text: Parabolic SAR, a stop below the lows in an uptrend and above the highs in a downtrend: a bar across it changes the trend, and the first trend is up if the second close is higher. It has no series argument, and its speed increases by step at each new high or low, from step to max (step cannot be more than max).
functions.example: buy when close crosses above psar()

functions.name: cmf
functions.summary: Chaikin money flow, -1 to 1
functions.text: Chaikin money flow, -1 to 1: the sum of ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume of the last n bars, divided by their volume. It has no series argument, the ticker must have volume, and a bar with no range adds 0.

functions.name: linreg
functions.summary: least-squares line, at this bar
functions.text: The value at this bar of the least-squares line through the last n values, with slope(n) as its slope per bar. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in linreg(volume, 20).

functions.name: rsquared
functions.summary: fit of a line to the last n values, 0 to 1
functions.text: R squared of the least-squares line through the last n values, 0 to 1 (1 when all are on a line), unknown for equal values. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in rsquared(volume, 20).

functions.name: efficiency
functions.summary: Kaufman efficiency ratio, 0 to 1 (1 for a straight move)
functions.text: Kaufman efficiency ratio, 0 to 1: |x - x[n]| divided by the sum of |x - x[1]| in the last n bars, unknown with no move. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in efficiency(volume, 20).
functions.example: buy when efficiency(20) > 0.3 and close > sma(50)

functions.name: streak
functions.summary: bars in a row up (1, 2, ...) or down (-1, -2, ...)
functions.text: Bars in a row the value increased (1, 2, 3, ...) or decreased (-1, -2, ...), 0 if it did not change, unknown on the first bar. It reads close, or the series you write first, as in streak(volume), and after an unknown value it is unknown until the next known change.

functions.name: min
functions.summary: the smaller value
functions.text: The smaller of two values.

functions.name: max
functions.summary: the larger value
functions.text: The larger of two values.

functions.name: abs
functions.summary: value without its sign
functions.text: The value without its sign.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.summary: square root
functions.text: The square root of the value, unknown for a value less than 0.

functions.name: log
functions.summary: natural logarithm
functions.text: The natural logarithm of the value, unknown for 0 or less.

functions.name: exp
functions.summary: e to the power x
functions.text: e to the power of the value, unknown when the result is too large.

functions.name: if
functions.summary: a where the condition holds, b where it does not
functions.text: The number a where the condition holds and b where it does not, or unknown where the condition is unknown. a and b are numbers, not conditions.

functions.name: column
functions.summary: a column of a CSV file: column(score) of signals
functions.text: Reads a numeric column of a CSV file by its header in lowercase, with underscores for spaces, for example column(score) of signals. A row counts as known at the close of its date.

series.name: open
series.text: The open price of each bar of the ticker of the rule. Yahoo adjusts prices for splits and dividends: compare them with an average, not with a constant number.

series.name: high
series.text: The highest price of each bar of the ticker of the rule. Yahoo adjusts prices for splits and dividends: compare them with an average, not with a constant number.

series.name: low
series.text: The lowest price of each bar of the ticker of the rule. Yahoo adjusts prices for splits and dividends: compare them with an average, not with a constant number.

series.name: close
series.text: The close price of each bar of the ticker of the rule. Yahoo adjusts prices for splits and dividends: compare them with an average, not with a constant number.

series.name: volume
series.text: The traded volume of each bar of the ticker of the rule.

calendar.name: month
calendar.text: The month of the bar, 1 to 12. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: day
calendar.text: The day of the month, 1 to 31. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: weekday
calendar.text: The day of the week: 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: year
calendar.text: The year, for example 2024. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: month_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a month. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: month_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a month. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: quarter
calendar.text: The quarter of the year of the bar, 1 to 4. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: week_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a week, which starts on Monday. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: week_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a week, which starts on Monday. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: quarter_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a quarter. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: quarter_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a quarter. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: year_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a year. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: year_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a year. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: trading_day
calendar.summary: number of the day in its month, of the days with a bar
calendar.text: The day number in the month, of days with a bar: 1 on the month’s first such day, unknown in the data’s first month. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

calendar.name: trading_days_left
calendar.summary: remaining days with a bar in the month
calendar.text: Days with a bar after this day in its month, 0 on the month’s last such day: after the last bar, holidays also count. The plugin reads it from the date of each bar, in UTC.

position.name: bars held
position.summary: completed bars since the entry filled, 0 on that bar
position.text: Completed bars since the buy filled, or the short sale (the first of more entries): it is 0 on the bar of the fill. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.

position.name: entry price
position.summary: the price the position was bought or sold short at
position.text: The price the position was bought at, slippage included, or for a short the price it was sold at (for more entries, the average). Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.

position.name: last entry price
position.summary: the price of the last entry
position.text: The fill price of the last entry of the position, slippage included, and with one entry, the same as entry price. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when close < last entry price * 0.95

position.name: entries made
position.summary: how many entries the position has
position.text: The number of entries of the open position: 1 after the buy or short sale, plus 1 for each add. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when entries made == 1 and bars held >= 10

position.name: highest since entry
position.summary: the highest price since the first entry
position.text: The maximum of the first fill price before slippage and each next high (and the fill bar high for a fill at its open). Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when close < highest since entry - 3 * atr(22)

position.name: lowest since entry
position.summary: the lowest price since the first entry
position.text: The minimum of the first fill price before slippage and each next low (and the fill bar low for a fill at its open). Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example:
short when close < sma(200)
cover when close > lowest since entry + 3 * atr(22)

position.name: position return
position.summary: the open position’s return at this close, before costs
position.text: The open position's return at this close before costs: close / entry price - 1 for a long, 1 - close / entry price for a short. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not in a function, in a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when position return > 20% or bars held > 30

settings.name: name
settings.summary: title shown above the result
settings.text: The title shown above the result. Without it, the title is Backtest.

settings.name: universe
settings.summary: tickers and weights: SPY 60%, TLT 40%
settings.text: The tickers to trade, each with an optional weight: give a weight to all tickers or to none. The maximum total weight is 200%: below 100%, the remaining weight stays in cash, and above 100%, the strategy borrows.

settings.name: symbol
settings.summary: one ticker (same as universe)
settings.text: The same as universe.

settings.name: from
settings.summary: first day, as 2015-01-31
settings.text: The first day of the run. Without it, the run starts on the first day that all tickers have prices.

settings.name: to
settings.summary: last day, as 2024-12-31
settings.text: The last day of the run, all of that day included, and it must be after from. Without it, the run ends on the last day with prices.

settings.name: data
settings.summary: where tickers without a prefix come from: yahoo, binance or tiingo
settings.text: The source of tickers without a prefix (if there is no data line, the plugin setting is the source). A ticker that starts with ^ always comes from Yahoo, and a prefix (yahoo:, binance:, tiingo:, fred: or csv:) sets the source of one ticker.

values.summary: Yahoo prices, adjusted for splits and dividends
values.text: Tickers without a prefix come from Yahoo: write them as Yahoo does, for example SPY, BRK-B, BTC-USD or ^GSPC. Yahoo gives 1d and 1w bars.

values.summary: Binance market symbols, for example BTCUSDT
values.text: Tickers without a prefix are Binance market symbols, for example BTCUSDT, but a ticker that starts with ^ (for example ^VIX) comes from Yahoo. Binance gives bars from 1m to 1w.

values.summary: Tiingo prices, adjusted for splits and dividends
values.text: Tickers without a prefix come from Tiingo, with the key from the Tiingo API key setting, but tickers that start with ^ come from Yahoo. Tiingo gives 1d and 1w bars of US stocks, ETFs and funds.

settings.name: interval
settings.summary: bar size: 1d, 1w, or 1h and others on Binance
settings.text: The bar size for all tickers, 1d if you do not write it. Yahoo and Tiingo give 1d and 1w bars, and Binance gives bars from 1m to 1w.

values.text: 1-minute bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
3-minute bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
5-minute bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
15-minute bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
30-minute bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
1-hour bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
2-hour bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
4-hour bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
6-hour bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
8-hour bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
12-hour bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
Daily bars, from Yahoo, Tiingo or Binance.
3-day bars, only from Binance. The block must have data: binance or a binance: ticker.
Weekly bars, from Yahoo, Tiingo or Binance. The plugin uses a weekly bar only after its week ends.

settings.name: capital
settings.summary: capital at the start, as 10000 or 10k
settings.text: The capital at the start of the run, as 10000 or 10k (m is millions). Without it, the plugin uses its Start capital setting.

settings.name: costs
settings.summary: cost of each trade, as 5 bps or 0.05%
settings.text: The cost of each trade, as 5 bps or 0.05%. A number without a unit counts as bps, and the cost must be less than 10%.

settings.name: slippage
settings.summary: how much worse each fill is than the price, as 5 bps
settings.text: How much worse each fill is than the price: a buy or a cover fills higher, and a sell or a short sale fills lower. Write it as you write costs.

settings.name: size
settings.summary: share of equity to use when tickers have no weights
settings.text: The share of equity to use when the tickers have no weights, a maximum of 200%: above 100%, the strategy borrows. You cannot use weights and size together.

settings.name: rebalance
settings.signature: rebalance: never | weekly | monthly | quarterly | yearly
settings.summary: never, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly
settings.text: How frequently the strategy sets the held tickers back to their weights. Without it, the value is never.

values.text: The strategy does not set held positions back to their weights. This is the default.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each week
values.text: The strategy sets each held ticker back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new week. Weeks start on Monday.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each month
values.text: The strategy sets each held ticker back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new month. A rebalance does not open a position.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each quarter
values.text: The strategy sets each held ticker back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new quarter. A rebalance does not open a position.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each year
values.text: The strategy sets each held ticker back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new year. A rebalance does not open a position.

settings.name: benchmark
settings.summary: ticker to compare with, bought and held
settings.text: The ticker to compare the result with, bought and held. Without it, the benchmark is the tickers of the block at their weights.

settings.name: stop loss
settings.summary: sell this far below the entry price (above it for a short), as 10% or 2 atr(14)
settings.text: Sells when the price moves this far below the entry price, or covers a short when the price moves this far above it. Write a percentage, more than 0% and a maximum of 99%, or a number of average true ranges.

settings.name: trailing stop
settings.summary: sell this far below the highest price since entry (above the lowest for a short)
settings.text: Sells when the price moves this far below the highest price since entry, or covers a short when it moves this far above the lowest. A percentage must be more than 0% and a maximum of 99%.

settings.name: take profit
settings.summary: sell this far above the entry price (below it for a short)
settings.text: Sells when the price moves this far above the entry price, or covers a short when it moves this far below it. A percentage must be more than 0% and a maximum of 1000%, and for a short, a take profit of 100% or more cannot occur.

settings.name: cash rate
settings.summary: interest on cash: 4% a year, or a yield ticker, for example ^IRX
settings.text: The yearly interest on cash: a rate, as 4%, or a ticker with a yearly yield as its close, for example ^IRX or fred:DGS3MO. A rate must have its percent sign, and the maximum is 50%.

settings.name: borrow fee
settings.summary: yearly fee on the value of short positions, default 0.5%
settings.text: A yearly fee on the value of each short position at the close, for each day of the position, included in the trade’s return. Without it, the plugin uses its Borrow fee for shorts setting (default 0.5%), and the fee must be between 0% and 100%.

settings.name: margin rate
settings.summary: yearly interest on borrowed money, default 6%
settings.text: Yearly interest on borrowed money: the strategy pays it between two bars when cash minus the shorts is less than 0, for example with leverage. Without it, the plugin uses its Interest on borrowed money setting (default 6%), and the rate must be between 0% and 50%.

settings.name: test from
settings.summary: show results before this day and from this day apart
settings.text: Shows the results before this day and from this day apart. It is one run, divided in two with no new fit, and the day must be after from and before to.

settings.name: hold
settings.summary: hold only the tickers with the highest score: top 3 by roc(126)
settings.text: Holds only the tickers with the highest score, for example the top 3 by roc(126). Write the score as a value in a rule, and give no weights in the universe.

settings.name: weighting
settings.summary: inverse volatility(60): less volatility, more weight
settings.text: Tickers with less volatility receive more weight: each weight is in proportion to 1 divided by the volatility of the last n one-bar returns. The minimum period is 2.

settings.name: risk per trade
settings.summary: size each buy or short sale by its risk: 1% at 2 atr(14)
settings.text: Sizes each buy or short sale: a move of that many average true ranges against it costs that share of equity (maximum: the ticker’s weight). You cannot use it with weighting, or with a rebalance other than never.

settings.name: fill
settings.summary: when orders fill: at the next open, or at the same close
settings.text: When the orders from the rules fill. With next open (the default), an order at the close of a bar fills at the next open, and with close, at that close.

values.summary: an order at a close fills at the next open
values.text: An order at the close of a bar fills at the next open of that ticker. This is the default.

values.summary: an order at a close fills at that same close
values.text: An order at the close of a bar fills at that same close.

settings.name: commission
settings.summary: charge for each order: 1, or 0.005 per share, min 1, max 1%
settings.text: A charge in the account currency: a constant value for each order, or a value per share with an optional minimum and maximum. The plugin adds it to costs, the maximum is a percentage of the order value, and without it, the plugin setting (default none) applies.

settings.name: entries
settings.summary: open each position in a maximum of 3 entries, one third each
settings.text: Opens each position in a maximum of that many equal entries: the buy rule makes the first, and the add rule makes the others. It must have an add rule, and the entries together are not more than the ticker’s weight.
settings.example:
entries: 3
add when close > last entry price * 1.03

settings.name: magnify
settings.summary: read stops and targets on 1h bars in each bar
settings.text: Reads stops and targets on smaller bars in each bar to find which one the price touches first, but rules use the strategy bars. Yahoo gives 2m to 1h bars in daily bars for the last 60 days (730 for 1h), and 1d bars in weekly bars.

words.name: between
words.summary: in a range, the two ends included
words.text: True when a is lo or more and hi or less: rsi(2) between 10 and 30 is rsi(2) >= 10 and rsi(2) <= 30. It is one comparison that does not chain: not rsi(2) between 10 and 30 is true when rsi(2) is not in the range.

words.name: for … bars
words.summary: held on each of the last n bars
words.text: True when the condition held on each of the last n bars, this bar included, and unknown until all n are known. It applies to the comparison before it and to a not in front of that (not up for 3 bars is (not up) for 3 bars): use brackets for more.
words.example: buy when close > sma(200) for 3 bars

words.name: within
words.summary: held on one or more of the last n bars
words.text: True when the condition held on one or more of the last n bars, this bar included, and unknown until all n are known. n is an integer from 1 to 10000 or a parameter, and you can also write bar.

words.name: buy when
words.summary: condition that opens a long position
words.text: Opens a long position in a ticker that the strategy does not hold when the condition is true at a close. It fills at the next open of that ticker, unless fill is close.

words.name: sell when
words.summary: condition that closes a long position
words.text: Closes a long position when the condition is true at a close. Without a sell rule, the strategy holds a position until a stop or a short rule closes it, or until the run ends.

words.name: add when
words.summary: condition that adds the next entry
words.text: Adds the next entry to the open position, long or short, when the condition is true at a close, up to the number in entries. It must have an entries line, and the plugin ignores it at a close where the sell rule (for a short, the cover rule) holds.
words.example:
entries: 3
add when close > last entry price * 1.03

words.name: short when
words.summary: condition that opens a short position
words.text: Sells short a ticker that the strategy does not hold when the condition is true at a close, and fills as a buy does. It also closes a long position in the ticker, and opens the short at the same fill if the buy rule does not hold there.

words.name: cover when
words.summary: condition that closes a short position
words.text: Buys a short position back when the condition is true at a close, and it must have a short rule. Without a cover rule, the strategy holds a short until a stop or the buy rule closes it, or until the run ends.
words.example:
short when close < sma(200)
cover when close > sma(200)

words.name: for
words.summary: rules and stops for one or more tickers: for TLT:
words.text: Starts rules for one ticker, or for more tickers with commas between them (for SPY, TLT:), and each must be in the universe. A buy, sell, short, cover or add rule, stop loss, trailing stop or take profit below it replaces the shared one for those tickers only.

words.name: for all
words.summary: back to the rules that all tickers share
words.text: Goes back to the rules that all tickers share. The lines after it apply to all tickers, but a rule in a for section replaces the shared rule for its tickers.

words.name: and
words.summary: the two conditions hold
words.text: True when the two conditions are true. A rule can continue on the next line: indent the line and start it with and or or.
words.example: buy when close > sma(200) and rsi(14) < 70

words.name: or
words.summary: one or more of the conditions hold
words.text: True when one or more of the conditions are true. The plugin applies it last: a and b or c is (a and b) or c.
words.example: sell when close < sma(200) or rsi(14) > 85

words.name: not
words.summary: the condition does not hold
words.text: True when the condition after it is not true. The plugin applies it after a comparison and before and: not close > 1 is not (close > 1), and not up for 3 bars is (not up) for 3 bars.

words.name: crosses
words.summary: crossed above or below
words.text: True on a bar where a crosses b: a is not on the same side of b as on the previous bar. Write crosses above or crosses below for one direction only.

words.name: crosses above
words.summary: was at or below, then above
words.text: True on a bar where a is above b and was at or below b on the previous bar.
words.example: buy when sma(50) crosses above sma(200)

words.name: crosses below
words.summary: was at or above, then below
words.text: True on a bar where a is below b and was at or above b on the previous bar.
words.example: sell when sma(50) crosses below sma(200)

words.name: above
words.summary: same as >
words.text: The same as >. You can also write is above.

words.name: below
words.summary: same as <
words.text: The same as <. You can also write is below.

words.name: of
words.summary: a value of a different ticker: sma(200) of SPY
words.text: Reads a value from a different ticker, in the universe or not. For each bar, it reads the ticker’s last bar that ended at or before the end of this bar.
words.example: buy when close > sma(200) and close of ^VIX < 25

words.name: tiingo:
words.summary: a ticker from Tiingo, for example tiingo:SPY
words.text: Downloads the daily prices of this ticker from Tiingo, adjusted for splits and dividends, with the key from the Tiingo API key setting. Tiingo gives 1d and 1w bars of US stocks, ETFs and funds.

words.name: fred:
words.summary: a FRED data series, for example fred:T10Y2Y
words.text: A series from FRED, with each value from the day FRED first published it and the key from the FRED API key setting. Rules read it with of, and cash rate can use it as a yield (fred:DGS3MO), but you cannot trade it or make it the benchmark.

words.name: [n]
words.summary: the value n bars before: close[5]
words.text: The value n bars before this bar: close[5] is the close five bars before. It works on all values, and n must be an integer or a parameter with an integer value.

words.name: in … step
words.summary: a range for a sweep: 50 in 20..100 step 10
words.text: Gives a parameter a range of values for a sweep, but the block runs with the value before in, which must be in the range. The step is optional: without it, the step is 1, or 1% for a percentage.

words.name: top … by
words.summary: hold the 3 tickers with the highest score
words.text: In hold: the number of tickers to hold, and the score that sets their sequence, written as a value in a rule. The universe must have that number of tickers or more.

words.name: at
words.summary: share of equity at risk for a stop distance
words.text: In risk per trade: the word between the share of equity at risk and the move against the position, in average true ranges.

words.name: true
words.summary: always holds
words.text: A condition that always holds. You can also write always.

words.name: false
words.summary: does not hold
words.text: A condition that does not hold. You can also write never.

units.text: A percentage. It counts as the number 0.05 where you can write a number: roc(20) > 5% is roc(20) > 0.05.

units.name: bps
units.text: Basis points: hundredths of a percent, thus 100 bps is 1%. In costs and slippage, a number without a unit also counts as bps.

laterWords.about: Words added after 0.7.0. A block may still use one as a parameter or definition name, which it then means in that block; calling it as a function there is an error.
